questions.stem: The page mentions chip cards once. In what context does it mention them?

options.says: The page's account of 1993 speaks of new and refined data elements; chip cards appear only under 2003.

options.text: As one of the transaction types the standard supports
options.says: The transaction types the page names are purchases, cash withdrawals, refunds and balance inquiries; chip cards are not among them.

options.text: As something the 2003 version added support for
options.says: Section 1.2.3 lists support for new transaction types and technologies among what the 2003 version added, with chip cards as its example.

options.text: As a technology whose adoption the standard speeds up
options.says: The page's point about faster adoption across regions names no technology; chip cards appear only under 2003.

questions.stem: The page says the 1993 version's changes were meant to better support evolving transaction types and security requirements. Where else on the page does security come up?

options.text: Among the ways the standard ensures interoperability between institutions
options.says: The page's interoperability list covers communication, cross-border use, new players and value-added services; none is about security.
Section 1.2.3 lists enhancing security features to address emerging threats among what the 2003 version added.

options.text: In the page's statement of the standard's primary purpose
options.says: The page states the purpose as a common interface for exchanging electronic transactions between financial systems, with no word on security.

options.text: Among the reasons the standard matters for global standardization
options.says: The page's four reasons under global standardization are a common language, lower cost, faster adoption and consistent processing; none is about security.

questions.stem: The page credits ISO-8583 with faster adoption of new payment technologies across different regions. Which of the standard's benefits does it list that under?

options.says: The page's interoperability list is about communication between banks, cross-border use, new players and value-added services, not the adoption of new technologies.

options.text: Its role in electronic financial transactions
options.says: The page's list of roles covers a standardized format, structured data, real-time authorization, clearing and settlement, and the range of transaction types.
Section 1.3.1 lists faster adoption of new payment technologies across regions as one reason the standard matters for global standardization.

questions.stem: The page lists four roles ISO-8583 plays in electronic financial transactions. Which of these is one of the four?

options.text: Consistent processing and reporting on a global scale
options.says: The page lists that as a reason for global standardization, not among the four roles.

options.text: Seamless communication between banks, processors and networks
options.says: The page lists that under interoperability between financial institutions, not among the four roles.

options.text: A common language for financial institutions worldwide
options.says: The page lists that as a reason for global standardization, not among the four roles.

options.text: Structured, efficient transmission of complex transaction data
options.says: It is the second of the four roles in section 1.1.2.
